_doc: Tier judgments. tier: A accumulates | B living-but-unproven | C place/tool/material | D written record | E stub. verified: 'code' = file tree or source inspected, 'readme' = README read, 'meta' = description/size only. Repos absent from this file appear on the page as UNSORTED.

persistent-memory-substrate.why: One file. The repo contains the README and nothing else — the substrate is stated, never implemented. It remains the clearest statement of the criterion on the account, and it is a statement.

Keava-Owent.why: main.py assembles fifteen subsystems — store, continuity, loop, live-reference engine, consumption and contribution ledgers, memory graph, recall, spark generator, membrane, approval queue, receipts, transport. None of those modules are committed; the import fails on the first line. What is here is the assembly, the tests, and config/membrane.yaml — a human-owned permission file the system reads and can never write, which is a corrigibility guarantee made concrete. An architecture of unusual quality, and not a running system.

zeus-ai.why: 131 files: ledger, memory, heartbeat, workers, Docker. A local FastAPI/React workbench over Ollama with local RAG — plus a training/ path for from-scratch Zeus-Tiny weights. A small model with no datacenter, already started.

autonomous-agent-os.why: Two files. The README is explicit: the architecture is locked to a six-layer stack and “no production code is committed yet.” A design document for a system that would accumulate, not a system that does.

ai-heartbeat-engine.why: Seven files, all documentation. Describes a real self-continuing loop whose entire operating surface is prompts and scheduled tasks rather than code — so the loop may well run, but the repo is its specification, not its implementation.

pam-continuum.why: Live on Project Heartbeat: pam_instances, pam_devices, threads and messages all carry rows. Its pam_action_ledger is still empty — the control plane exists and is connected, and has not yet recorded an action.

ATOMIC-CHRONICLE-v4.0-A-World-You-Want-O.why: Real implementation in atomic_chronicle_v4.py — a neutral immutable ledger for actions and state across independent worlds, built for long-term continuity.

Atomic-World-Chronicle-3.7.why: A single 52KB implementation file named “ATOM Code 3.7”, no extension — which is why filename scans miss it. Immutable state tracking and cross-world interaction, actually written.

Atomic-Chronicle-Memory-Chain-.why: Working Python prototype: local blockchain ledger, tokenised wallet, an Asteroids-style game and an optional Arduino robot, where in-game actions commit blocks and trigger real-world commands. One ledger spanning a game and a machine.

ATOMIC-CHRONICLE-v4.0-A-world-you-want-o.why: Two files, README only. Duplicate shell of the v4.0 description with no implementation.

Summary-Of-repos-Memory-linker.why: A machine-readable map of the whole account built for Zeus, verified from fresh clones plus live Vercel and Supabase state — explicitly not from READMEs — and rendered as a Three.js data centre. Generated 2026-07-12 and never regenerated, which is precisely the failure it was built to avoid.

orchestra.why: Seventy-seven files around an append-only tracking/events.jsonl. Each cycle asks five AI systems eight questions, preserves every capture, hands the corpus to two synthesizers, and tracks falsifiable signals until they are confirmed, invalidated, decayed or left unresolved. It keeps its failures too.

accumulation-sort.why: This page. Re-reads the account every morning without being asked, appends what it found to history.jsonl, and never rewrites a prior line. It qualifies under its own criterion, which is the only reason it is allowed to apply it.

the-current.why: Verified in the running database, not just in code: the_current_era_archives holds a retired era and the_current_era_entropy holds 66 replay inputs kept with it. An era of this civilization has already ended and been preserved. Ticked server-side by a Supabase edge function, so it advances with every browser closed. The criterion satisfied in production.

livi-organism.why: The code carries Drizzle plus Supabase migrations for revisioned cloud memory and a cloud-persistence test suite — but no database on the account holds livi tables. The persistence is written and unapplied, so today the organism lives only in the browser it was opened in.

ashgrove-npc-online.why: The shared town is real in the database: world3_world holds the seed, founding plat, growth records, change log and a digest-verified snapshot, advanced only through world3_advance_day(). It retains — but nothing calls that function on a schedule, so the town only moves when someone moves it. Retention without continuation: exactly half the criterion.

rustfall.why: Roaming robots and an NPC job economy across 125 files, with a local save and five rustfall_* cloud tables standing empty. The world persists for one player on one device; the shared version is provisioned and unused.

fable-survival.why: Cloud save is implemented, and its Supabase project is INACTIVE — paused. Right now the cloud save cannot write, so what survives is whatever the browser kept.

The-Free-Online-Neighborhood-.why: Drizzle ORM, a worker and scheduled workflows — a shared neighbourhood with a real database behind it.

Pirate-World-Sea-Of-Fortune-.why: Supabase-backed in code; the project is INACTIVE and its tables were already empty when last inspected in July. The backend is provisioned, paused and unused.

AETHERSPAN-v1.1-Anonymous-Teleoperation-.why: 41KB of implementation in “AETHERSPAN CODE 1.1”. Bridges controller input to a real device and logs every action to an append-only hash-chained SQLite ledger.

Reflector-To-API-Bridges-.why: 14KB of implementation in “Reflector Code”. Translates domain commands into AETHERSPAN frames and hands back the response. Stateless by design.

heartbeat-observatory.why: 393 files. A shell that hosts other worlds rather than being one — the save systems and Supabase config inside it belong to the games it carries. Its charter includes a Live-Reference clause of its own: reality outranks text, amend rather than obey.

MindGames.why: Fifty files. A screen becomes a perspective-aware window, then a traversable portal — recursive worlds, cross-reality causality, scale shifts. Nothing retained between visits.

showcase-world.why: Material-first inspection-ready downtown: real photographed material maps on a deterministic grid with stable asset IDs and collision proxies. Built from Tessera and ModKit parts.

northstar-addressable-world.why: First-person parkour game and a proof of an addressable-world engine — every place in the world has a stable name.

wasteland-commons.why: Server-authoritative world state with restore and a live, healthy database — and every table has zero rows. Built to survive everyone leaving, and nobody has arrived yet.

surface-material-lab.why: 218 files. Turns real photographed surfaces into reusable inspectable material packages. Deliberately independent of the game repos — a materials library, not a world.

asset-pack-ue-threejs-blender-unity.why: ModKit: 38 CC0 modular building and prop assets, ~40.6k triangles, shipped as FBX, GLB and .blend for four engines.

tessera-worldkit.why: 230 files. An AI-readable world-building framework with a public workshop — ships the placement contract so agents stop guessing dimensions. The most reusable thing in this tier.

spectral-gt-rs.why: A procedural sports car authored in Blender, shipped with the editable source scene, a game-ready GLB and a browser drive test.

Movie-Theater-Three.js-Asset-.why: Theater asset with a Playwright test rig, feeding Heartbeat Observatory's cinema.

World-Printer-Lab-For-3D-Worlds.why: World generation lab with a version inventory.

worldbuilding-lab.why: Worldbuilding doctrine v2/v3 plus texture and manifest discipline. A style guide with a renderer attached.

SYL-Full-Game.why: World-scale space foundation: multiple planets, real surface-to-space traversal with no loading screens, modular ships, factions, and a local save/worldState pair. Written as a bridge for other agents to continue.

SpaceYouLand.why: 739 files of Unreal project with combat checkpoint volumes and a MEMORY.md for its agents. The engine-side slice of Space You Land.

SYL-Neighborhood.why: Two files. A walkable inspectable neighbourhood prototype on Tessera's principles — stable IDs, metric grid, one-key debug layer.

SYL-Testing-pvp.why: Nine files around a single server.js — a PvP test bed.

rift-clash.why: Server-authoritative 5v5 MOBA with a full bot roster, everything — champions, portraits, item icons, terrain, particles — generated at runtime. The match ends and the world ends with it.

Free-Game-Hub.why: 187 files behind a games.json index. A shelf, not a system.

Kurearthis.why: Unreal project with an accumulating BUILDLOG and archive, a world model and a charter. The build process keeps a record; the game does not.

cyber-trench-overdrive.why: Two files. A neon endless trench runner.

the-defender-3d.why: Courtroom strategy across opening, evidence, cross-examination, objection and closing phases, with a jury that visibly reacts.

the-necklace-show.why: An 86KB app.js behind a fifteen-chapter story about a necklace that reveals the memories held by objects — and a canonical-archive keeping the original one-prompt Kimi output, zip included, beside the version that grew from it. The never-delete pledge, applied inside a repo.

aetherforge-threejs-mod-studio.why: An asset and mod-pack editor around a rain-soaked ruin courtyard, explicit that it is a vertical slice rather than a claim to AAA volume.

cinematic-inspection-lab.why: Asset registry, constraints, grid, scene and sequence manifests, QA report — record-keeping as discipline, not runtime retention.

market-architect.why: TypeScript monorepo with vitest and no persistence layer.

Jaron-Game-World-Foundation.why: Shared foundation with a registry.json and agent instructions — a parts bin for the world projects.

Air-Vehicles-.why: Vite/TS flight vehicles, deployed to Vercel.

THE-SHIFTING.why: Vite/TypeScript app with a deploy workflow. No persistence.

vibecoding-training-grounds-.why: Newest repo on the account. Vite/TS with agent instructions and a deploy workflow.

direct-binary-emission-system.why: Deterministic byte emission and validation for PE, ELF, WASM, boot sectors and WAVE, with a memory module, a test suite and CI. An instrument with a conscience — but it holds nothing between runs.

Phone-AI-App-builds.why: Single index.html of phone-built apps behind a deploy workflow.

Framing-Lens.why: Thirteen files: a prompt set, scoring engine, data model, routes, policy model, wireflow and roadmap — plus a package.json declaring Next and React, and not one source file. The app is fully specified and unbuilt.

Pictures-screenshots.why: Three files: a gallery viewer, a README, and an empty imgs/ directory. The archive other projects were told to reference has no images in it, so those raw URLs resolve to nothing.

President-Sim.why: One 35KB index.html carrying twenty scenarios drawn from real 2025–26 events, each decision moving five pillars. Complete and self-contained.

reality-skin-engine.why: Design principles, system architecture, terminology and decision log — a specification with a skinning engine attached.

live-reference-principle.why: Constraints and signals are only valid while connected to what they reference; frozen references become gestures. The acceptance test for both tiers above, and the reason this page rebuilds itself.

THE-ENVIRONMENT-CONSTRAINT-INTELLIGENCE-.why: Intelligence as self-maintenance under constraint. Five testable predictions; the closing unfalsifiable argument is the weak part.

YES-NO-Environment-Perspective-You-Mysel.why: Twelve chapters, written Dec 2024 to Feb 2025, primarily for your children.

Perspective-Environmental-framework-Exer.why: Six ambiguous prompts where the choice is a decoy and the reasoning is the signal. Run across nine models — one of the few repos here that produced data.

memory-as-spatial-arrangement.why: A working hypothesis with sim_unit_distance_memory.py and recorded first results — research that actually ran. Implemented inside Keava-Owent.

emergence-structure-that-grows.why: The companion principle: structure in trained systems is grown and discovered rather than built. Explicitly the piece memory-as-spatial-arrangement draws on.

Emergence-Forge-By-GPT-5.6-Luna.why: A cellular-automata lab, conjecture lab and pattern miner with recorded results files. Research that produced output.

ai-workforce.why: Five files, all documentation. A procedure for running scheduled work through consumer AI apps with no server and no always-on machine — real, and described rather than implemented.

ai-workforce-xai-openai.why: Four files. The two-provider write-up of the same procedure.

Neuro-consciousness-and-chemistry-.why: “AGI won't come from perfect code or flawless hardware. It comes from a system learning to keep itself going under real constraints.” ECIH's thesis, stated three months before ECIH.

The-Engine-Of-Division-.why: Twenty-eight files with a table of contents and a live site — a complete free book on how rivalry became a default operating system across school, brands and politics. Published as a repo to avoid copyright.

THEY-NEVER-LEFT.why: A structured thought experiment, explicit up front that it claims no truth — only the most internally consistent alternative explanation for a set of observations.

The-Structural-Conflict.why: A geopolitical timeline from Ottoman Palestine to 2026, written to hold both perspectives at once.

theater-vs-record-trump-drug-clemency.why: Stated position against documented record, with dated figures and sourcing. The same theater-versus-record test the Live-Reference Principle applies to systems.

The-Thinking-Gym.why: Sixteen markdown files, no code. Exercises.

Orchestra-Financial-.why: Two files: README and licence. A placeholder for the financial arm of Orchestra.

signal-pebble-echo-2917.why: Three files. Reads, in full: “are you reading me yet”.

grok-test-dummy-penguin-2026.why: A connector test Grok made for itself. “Nothing serious here.”

heartbeat-test.why: Three files. A pulse check for the heartbeat engine.

Online-NPC-City-.why: Sixteen files around a single index.html — a scaffold of the living-town idea, superseded by ashgrove-npc-online.
